tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.reference: USP 2024 description and relative solubility; in-house specification

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:28

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg of powdered sample in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold steps to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent).
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:29

tests.procedure: Identification test (A): ignite about 0.5 (unit not stated, see openQuestions); the material chars and leaves a residue of iron oxide.
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:30

tests.procedure: Identification test (B): to 10 mL of a 1 in 100 solution of ferric ammonium citrate green add 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise; the solution darkens but no precipitate forms.
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:30

tests.procedure: Identification test (C): to 5 mL of a 1 in 100 solution of ferric ammonium citrate add 0.3 mL potassium permanganate TS and 4 mL mercuric sulphate TS; heat the mixture to boiling; a white precipitate forms.
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:30

tests.procedure: Sulfates (limit test): sample 100 mg dissolved in 1 mL 2.7 N hydrochloric acid, diluted with water to 30 mL; add 3 mL barium chloride TS and water to 50 mL. Standard: 0.31 mL of 0.020 N sulfuric acid diluted to 30 mL, with 3 mL barium chloride TS, to 50 mL. Turbidity in the sample after 10 min must not exceed the standard (NMT 0.3%).
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:31

tests.procedure: Acidity: dissolve 1 g sample in 100 mL water; measure with a calibrated pH meter; the solution must show an acidic medium.
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate Green.txt:32

tests.procedure: Arsenic by AAS: reference solutions 2, 4 and 6 ppm from 1000 ppm arsenic standard solution in water; sample 15 g dissolved in 50 mL water and 1 mL nitric acid, diluted to 100 mL with water. Arsenic hollow-cathode lamp, air-acetylene flame. Analytical wavelength and the calculation of the result are not stated.

details.sampleDiluent: 50 mL water + 1 mL nitric acid, to 100 mL
details.missingDetails: analytical wavelength and result calculation not stated

tests.procedure: Assay (iodometric titration): transfer about 1 g accurately weighed sample to a 250 mL conical flask; dissolve in 25 mL water and 5 mL hydrochloric acid; add 4 g potassium iodide, stopper, stand 15 min protected from light; add 100 mL water; titrate the liberated iodine with 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS using starch TS; perform a blank and correct. Each mL of 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate = 5.585 mg iron (Fe).

details.titrantStandardization: about 210 mg primary standard potassium dichromate (pulverised, dried), per STM standardization paragraph (see source line 26)
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate = 5.585 mg Fe
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / Wt; E.P = end point, eq.wt = equivalent weight of iron (Fe), F = titrant factor, Wt = sample weight (mg) (as written)
